lesson.title: Return Under Pressure
lesson.hook: Two connected choices. Watch what your first shot creates.
lesson.liveIntro: A fast serve is coming into your backhand. Your preparation window is small.

tp1A.name: What fits the reply you actually receive?
tp1A.sit: They reply to your backhand with depth. You have recovered into range.
tp1A.q: What fits the reply you actually receive?
opts: Height and depth through the middle
Force a narrow change of direction

lines.A: You keep a broad target and time to recover. Still in play.
lines.B: It lands in this illustration, but the narrow target gives away margin.

tp1A.take: The serve sets your preparation time. The next ball sets your next decision.
tp1A.payoff: The serve sets your preparation time. The next ball sets your next decision.
tp1A.principle: Read the pace. Give your return room, then recover.
tp1A.why: A fast serve rewards compact preparation and a generous target. These are two possible replies, not guaranteed outcomes. Read the depth and your balance again before changing direction.

tp1B.name: What fits the reply you actually receive?
tp1B.sit: Their earlier contact sends you wide to the forehand. You are still adjusting.
tp1B.q: What fits the reply you actually receive?
opts: Height and depth through the middle
Force a narrow change of direction

lines.A: You buy recovery time from the wider contact. Still in play.
lines.B: This one lands, but forcing the line while adjusting adds risk.

tp1.name: What does this serve give you time for?
tp1.sit: A fast serve is coming into your backhand. Your preparation window is small.
tp1.q: What does this serve give you time for?
opts: Compact return with depth through the middle

lines.A: Your deeper return keeps their next contact behind the baseline. Read the reply.
lines.B: The narrow return lands shorter here. They step in and send you wide.

pro.label: Read the contact and court
pro.moment: A compact block is useful when serve speed removes time; a fuller return becomes available when time permits.
pro.read: A fast serve rewards compact preparation and a generous target. These are two possible replies, not guaranteed outcomes. Read the depth and your balance again before changing direction.

drill.name: Two-ball read
drill.how: Alternate faster and slower serves to the same wing. Call “compact” or “time” before the return, then play one more ball.
